He explains why many academics feel threatened by the focus on teaching.
He highlights the importance of education for solving global problems and the moral imperative to improve education alongside rising tuition fees.

He poses the question: Where will the solutions to global problems come from?
He emphasizes the role of the Millennial generation in finding these solutions.
He argues that educational quality cannot improve if deviation from norms is not allowed.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Dr. Coward smiles briefly while mentioning the saying about sunlight being the best disinfectant, momentarily transitioning to a positive (hopeful) mood.

He stresses that the focus should be on the larger issues within the department and not on him personally.
He calls the question of his teaching ability a 'distracting question.'
He emphasizes the need for transparency and scrutiny of the math department's practices, particularly regarding large classes for non-math majors.

youtube_description:
Dr. Alexander Coward, a lecturer of mathematics at UC Berkeley, speaks out about the department's termination of his contract at the end of the academic term.

Coward reached a national audience last year when he sent his students in Math 1A an inspirational email about education that went viral. Now he is making headlines again by "blowing the whistle" on the math department.

Read his blog post here: http://alexandercoward.com/BlowingTheWhistleOnUCBerkeleyMathematics.html
